chapters.n: Jarom, Enos’s son, writes briefly as his father commanded, mainly to keep the family genealogy going.
The plates are small, and they are written for the future benefit of the Lamanites. Jarom won’t record his own revelations—his fathers have already taught the plan of salvation.

f.w: benefit of our brethren the Lamanites

chapters.n: Much effort was needed because the people were hard-hearted, spiritually deaf, blind, and stubborn. Still, God was merciful and spared them.
Not everyone was stubborn. Many had revelations, and those with faith enjoyed communion with the Holy Spirit.

f.g: Close fellowship and ongoing guidance by the Spirit.

chapters.n: After 200 years (about 400 BC), the Nephites were strong. They kept the law of Moses and the Sabbath, avoided profanity and blasphemy, and had strict laws.

f.g: Did not treat sacred things with disrespect.

chapters.n: Both peoples spread across the land. The Lamanites greatly outnumbered the Nephites and were violent.

f.g: Forbidden under the law of Moses (Leviticus 17:10-14).

chapters.n: The Lamanites attacked often, but Nephite kings and leaders were strong in faith and taught the people. The Nephites repelled them and fortified their cities.
The Nephites multiplied and prospered—gold, silver, fine woodwork, buildings, machinery, metals, tools, and weapons.

f.g: Mechanical devices or tools; the exact nature is not specified.

chapters.n: Well prepared, the Nephites held off the Lamanites. God’s promise was fulfilled: keep the commandments and prosper in the land.

f.w: ye shall prosper in the land

chapters.n: The prophets warned that if the Nephites fell into sin they would be destroyed.

f.w: destroyed from off the face of the land

chapters.n: Prophets, priests, and teachers labored patiently, teaching the purpose of the law of Moses and urging the people to believe in the coming Messiah “as though he already was.”
Their persistent preaching kept the people from destruction by “pricking their hearts” and stirring them to repentance.
Two hundred thirty-eight years had passed (about 362 BC), much of it marked by wars and divisions.

f.w: two hundred and thirty and eight years

chapters.n: Jarom stops, since the plates are small. The wars are detailed on the large plates, written by or for the kings.
Jarom passes the plates to his son Omni.
